topic: AI basics: what "tokens" and the "context window" are, in plain English
post:
Ever heard people talk about "tokens" and thought, huh? 🪙
Here are two AI words, explained in plain English.

1️⃣ Tokens
AI doesn't read words the way we do. It breaks text into small pieces called tokens. A token can be a whole word, part of a word, or even a single character.

So "unbelievable" might be a few tokens, not one.

2️⃣ The context window
Anthropic describes it as the model's "working memory": the amount of text Claude can look back on while it writes your answer.

It's different from what Claude learned in training. It's what's in front of it right now: your messages, its replies, and any files you share. 📄

Think of it like a desk 🗂️
Training is everything Claude studied. The context window is the desk it's working at. The more you pile on, the more crowded it gets.

Try this when a chat gets long:
"Summarize the key decisions and facts from this chat in 5 bullets, so I can start a fresh chat with them."

Why it matters:
Once you know Claude works from a "desk", you'll share the right files, keep chats focused, and get sharper answers. 💡
